-- **Fixture projects are linted for correctness only.** `projects/**` and `project-fixtures/**` are sample user apps, and snapshots assert on line and column numbers inside them, so `eslint.config.ts` turns off every rule whose `meta.type` is `layout` (computed from `baseConfig`, so a layout rule added there later is off here too), stops reporting unused `eslint-disable` directives (deleting one moves every line below it), and turns off rules that flag ordinary user-app code. `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` is off as well: Angular resolves a constructor parameter's type to a DI token at runtime, so a type-only import breaks the app. So is `cypress/no-unnecessary-waiting`: fixture specs wait on purpose to produce the timings, videos, command logs and mid-wait errors that system tests assert on. Files that fail to parse on purpose are in `ignores`, and fixture `package.json` files are left out of `jsonConfig` because they mirror the projects they stand in for. Don't run a bulk `eslint --fix` over the fixtures to clear a new rule; fix each violation by hand and rerun the affected system tests.

- **A local run prunes snapshot keys for tests that did not run.** `snap-shot-it` removes stored snapshots it did not see during a local (non-CI) run, so `yarn test web_security --browser chrome` deletes the Firefox- and Electron-gated keys from `__snapshots__/web_security_spec.js`, and CI then fails those tests with `Cannot store new snapshot value`. After any local system-test run, restore the snapshots before committing (`git checkout -- system-tests/__snapshots__`), and never stage with `git add -A` right after one.
